subject: Re: [acme/widget-service] docs: ask for a plain-language summary in descriptions (PR #34)
plainBody:
@lee-m commented on this pull request.

> +* Open with a plain-English summary, before any heading: two short
+ paragraphs, "what was broken" then "what this does".

I think the two examples actually agree with each other — and give us a clean split. One style is what-first for the *subject line*, and in a pull request that role is played by the *title*.

So: title says what it does; description opens problem-first. Does that work for you?

subject: Re: [acme/widget-service] store: drain work before close (PR #56)
plainBody:
@sam-k commented on this pull request.

Thanks!

Apologies for not approving. I hope you were not waiting for that.

Some comments, nothing major.

> @@ -358,6 +359,9 @@ func (c *Client) Address(repo, branch, path string) (string, error)

 func (c *Client) Close() error {
 	var errs error
+	// Drain background work before closing what it runs on.
+	c.pool.StopAndWait()

# :+1:

Good catch!

> +// A fold that cancels out entirely must leave the branch clean rather than
+// publish a range that only reproduces the head.

I cannot see what this can test. There is no functional requirement: the id is a hash of its contents.

The only thing it might do is detect that nothing happened. And that's an _implementation_ test.

> +
+	_, err := s.Store.Put(ctx, key, value)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	before, err := s.Manager.Get(ctx, key)
+	require.NoError(t, err)

Uggh. I guess that's because leases don't lead to durable locks. Consider opening an issue like

> ## Leases do not durably lock so the test cannot detect failures

@kim-t WDYT?

--
